naslov: Yusuf Is Thrown into the Well

segmenti.tekst: نحن نقص عليك أحسن القصص بما أوحينا إليك هذا القرآن وإن كنت من قبله لمن الغافلين. الحمد لله رب العالمين، والصلاة والسلام على نبينا محمد وعلى آله وصحبه أجمعين. And when Yusuf's brothers hatched a plan to get rid of Yusuf, alayhis-salatu was-salam,
they went to his father, saying: “Qalu ya abana ma laka la ta'manna 'ala Yusufa wa inna lahu la nasihun” – “Our father, why do you distrust us concerning Yusuf?

Why do you doubt our love for him, when we,” they said, “wish him nothing but good? Send him with us tomorrow, let him play a little, let him enjoy himself a little, and we,” they said, “will guard him, we will guard him.” So here, as we said yesterday, is proof that they had tried several times to take Yusuf, alayhis-salam, with them. That is, they had tried several times to take Yusuf, alayhis-salam,

with them. After all, dear brothers, he is their brother. After these words Ya'qub could not find any excuse not to let him go with them, but he warned them with the words: “Qala inni la yahzununi an tadhhabu bihi.”

He said: “Indeed,” he said, “it grieves me that he should go with you.” Why? Because he was small. We also mentioned that Ya'qub cared for him more than for the other brothers, because his mother had passed away.

So he did not like to be separated from him. He was small. The second thing, he says… And he says: “I fear that a wolf will eat him.” Because in those pastures where they tended the livestock there were many wolves that attacked the livestock.

So Ya'qub feared that the wolves would tear him apart while they were busy, that is, while his brothers were busy with play, amusement, and so on, and so forth. If we analyze these verses more closely, dear brothers, we will see here that Ya'qub unintentionally gave them the idea of how to find an excuse,
how to find an excuse if something happened to him. He says: “I fear that the wolves will eat him” – which they would later make use of.

The persuasion did not stop there, and they continued to persuade their father. “Qalu la'in akalahu adh-dhi'bu wa nahnu 'usbatun inna idhan la khasirun.” He says, that is, they say: “By Allah, if a wolf,” they said, “eats him, while we are,” they said, “such a big group, ten of us grown men, ten of us grown men,” they said, “if the wolves eat him,” they said, “then there is no khayr in us at all, no good at all, [unclear].”
That is impossible to happen. How they tried to persuade Ya'qub! In the end Ya'qub, alayhis-salatu was-salam, agreed to send Yusuf with them. As we said, after all, they are his brothers.

Ya'qub feared that his refusal, that his refusal – if he again forbade Yusuf to go out with them – would become the cause of even greater hatred. So he sent him, sent him with them. And when Ya'qub sent him, they went off with him. When they had disappeared from view and left the settlement,

they reached those pastures, agreed and gathered together to throw him to the bottom of a well, and they threw him to the bottom of the well. And we said, dear brothers, that the cause of this sin was envy. But not only envy. Shaykh Ibn al-Qayyim says: all the sins of people go back to three things, to three causes.

The first cause is envy, the second is greed, and the third is arrogance, arrogance, kibr. And all three of these things came together in Yusuf's brothers. They had envy toward Yusuf, jealousy; greed – that their father's love should belong only to them; and they were arrogant. That is, they were arrogant.

They said: “We are a big group, we are strong, we are stronger.” So, as we said, we see that here all three of these things were gathered precisely in them. And this led them to – what? – to commit this, this unbelievable, unbelievable sin.

What does Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala (glorified and exalted is He), say next, when they had thrown Yusuf and he was at the bottom of the well? He says… So, He says, while he was in the well, He says: “We revealed to him that you will inform them of this plot, of what they have done to you, while,” He says, “they will not even perceive it.” And you will see later how Yusuf will inform them of this plot, of this deception they set up against him. Also, dear brothers, what does
this verse indicate, as the scholars say? How did Allah reveal to Yusuf when he had not yet been sent as a prophet?
Some scholars say that Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, sent down security into his heart, sent down security and tranquility, so that Yusuf knew one hundred percent that he would get out of there.

Secondly, they say that He sent him an angel, who informed him of what would happen later. Also, dear brothers, here there is a beautiful lesson, as the scholars say: when Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, is with you, no one can do anything to you.

And when Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, is against you, is there any hope, is there any hope for such a person against whom Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, is? Also, a very, very, very important thing and a very important benefit, dear brothers: when something bad happens to us,
a person must not immediately rush to think that it is something bad and that Allah does not love him, that Allah wants to punish him, and so on. We see Yusuf, alayhis-salatu was-salam:
his brothers threw him into a well. An important Shari'ah principle, the scholars say: “Idha aradallahu shay'an hayya'a asbabahu.”
When Allah wills something, He prepares its causes. So what preceded Yusuf's elevation in this world and in the Hereafter?

His being thrown into the well. Had they not thrown him into the well, he would not have attained that rank, that degree which he attained. Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, says: “وَعَسَى أَنْ تَكْرَهُوا شَيْئًا وَهُوَ خَيْرٌ لَكُمْ” [unclear] “وَعَسَى أَنْ تُحِبُّوا شَيْئًا وَهُوَ شَرٌّ لَكُمْ” [unclear] “وَاللَّهُ يَعْلَمُ وَأَنْتُمْ لَا تَعْلَمُونَ” – He says: Allah knows, and you do not know. Also, a person should think well of Allah when something bad

happens to him, and entrust himself to Allah, as Yusuf entrusted himself. What does the Prophet, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam (peace be upon him), say? The Prophet says: Allah says: “Ana 'inda zanni 'abdi bi” – He says: “I am as My servant thinks of Me, according to the opinion My servant has of Me. So if My servant thinks well of Me, it will be well for him.

If he thinks ill of Me, it will surely, it will surely be ill for him.” That is why a person should think well of his, of his Lord, as Yusuf did, so that Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, after that, after that may help him and raise him up.

I ask Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, to reward you with every good. I ask Him, the Exalted, to forgive us our sins and the sins of our parents. I ask Him, the Exalted, to help us fast this month of Ramadan. Amin, ya Rabb al-alamin.
